title: Fix the Missing Super Constructor Call
description: The program should create an Employee that requires a Person's name to be provided.
expectedBehavior: The program should compile, and e.name should reflect the name passed up to Person's constructor.
actualProblem: Person has no no-argument constructor, only one requiring a String. Since Employee's constructor doesn't explicitly call super(...), Java tries to insert an implicit no-arg super() call, which doesn't exist — this is a compile error: 'constructor Person in class Person cannot be applied to given types'.
explanation: If a parent class has no no-argument constructor, every subclass constructor must explicitly call super(...) with matching arguments as its very first statement, so the parent's fields are properly initialized.
